I really enjoyed Tomb Raider 2013. My qualms with it were the gruesome deaths - seemed too many too often. Also the idea of Lara confronting her first human kill was a hugely dramatic moment. A moment which she became immune to within hours as she continued to slaughter hundreds of other men with no second thought.

I understand some of these things are just thing we have to suspend disbelief on when playing a game, and while playing it I definitely enjoyed it. These are things that bothered me afterwards, though.

As far as the Rise of the Tomb Raider is concerned, I am very excited about it, especially the fact that there will be much more "tomb raiding" and less "gruesome deaths" (as per developer interview)

A moment which she became immune to within hours as she continued to slaughter hundreds of other men with no second thought.

Yeah, I would've liked if the combat was less shooter-y (though I'm not quite sure exactly what I'd prefer) so that killing enemies is more impactful. It would've been awesome if you only kill 15 or 20 dudes throughout the entire game, cus to someone who's never killed anyone before, killing 15 or 20 people would probably feel like killing way more than that.

I liked how Lara could lose her grip and you have to hit a button quickly before you fall off of whatever you're holding on to, and I like the way some of the environments start to fall apart as you traverse them. However, like with a lot of QTEs, so many of them felt like cheap, stupid deaths that they kinda took me out of the game. When I think I'm watching a cutscene, I generally want to sit back and watch the damn cutscene. The quicktime events are my only major complaint about the game.

I never played the original, but I played 2 and 3 a pretty good amount. I also (unfortunately) played a ton of Angel of Darkness, which is total garbage.

2013 is really good, IMO. Good enough that I'm pretty excited for the next one. However, the story did feel rather unbalanced to me. The majority of it is a story of survival and conquering of adversity, and then it takes a weird, supernatural turn right toward the end. I know that this isn't exactly unheard of in the Tomb Raider franchise (the dagger in TR2 that when stabbed into someone's heart transforms them into a dragon), and I don't really have any ideas for other directions the story could have taken at the end, but still... Felt a little odd.
